name: CA-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic Los Angeles-area seat
Incumbent Laura Friedman running with a large financial edge ($469K on hand vs. $2.6K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at about 96%
No general-election polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Friedman: a D+21 district, incumbency, and a massive fundraising advantage over Scott Meyers, whose campaign has almost no cash. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at a roughly 25-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Friedman or an unusually favorable Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Laura Friedman, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Los Angeles-area district that voted about 21 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. She advanced to the general election and faces Republican Scott Meyers, a little-funded challenger with only a few thousand dollars on hand.

Friedman has raised over $800,000 and holds a cash advantage of more than $460,000, with no outside groups opposing her. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put her chances around 96 percent. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
